s: Streams row-level changes from database write-ahead logs to downstream systems with second-level freshness.
w: Debezium-style connectors read binlog/WAL, convert changes to structured events (before/after rows, op type), and publish to Kafka-compatible topics. Snapshot phase bootstraps existing table state then transitions to streaming. Schema registry handles column evolution; transforms filter/route. Downstream consumers rebuild caches/search indexes/analytics continuously.
use: Cache invalidation feeds keeping redis fresh within seconds
Search index sync (postgres -> elasticsearch without dual-writes)
Audit trails capturing every row change immutably
Warehouse micro-batch ingestion replacing nightly dumps
avoid: Transform-heavy ETL logic (pair with stream processor instead)
Sources you can't enable logical decoding on

pat.d: CDC reads committed rows directly - no outbox table needed.

pits: Replication slot bloat halts WAL recycling if consumer down - monitor lag + slot sizes
Schema drift breaks deserialization - evolve contracts via registry first
tips: Explain why log-based beats trigger/polling approaches (no source load, ordered, complete)
